name: Helper Functions Demo
description: Showcase the pre-loaded helper functions: data loading, export, visualization, and utilities.

cells.code:
# Show current AWS identity and environment
info = whoami()

## 📦 Data Loading

Load data from local files, S3, DynamoDB, or URLs — all in one line.

# Load a built-in sample dataset
# Call with no args to see available datasets
df = sample_data('orders')
print(f"Loaded {len(df)} rows")
df.head()

# Read CSV directly from S3 (uses the execution role — no credentials needed)
bucket = info['bucket']
clickstream = read_s3_csv(bucket, "samples/clickstream_events.csv")
print(f"Loaded {len(clickstream)} rows from S3")
clickstream.head()

# Read from DynamoDB (scans the table into a DataFrame)
reviews = read_dynamodb("ecommerce-reviews")
print(f"DynamoDB: {len(reviews)} items")
reviews.head()

# Fetch data from a public URL
iris = read_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv")
print(f"Iris dataset: {iris.shape}")
iris.head()

## 🔧 Utilities

Profile, compare, explore — all without boilerplate.

# Profile a DataFrame: types, nulls, unique values
profile(clickstream)

# List objects in an S3 bucket
files = list_s3(info['bucket'], "samples/")
files

# @param {"type": "slider", "min": 1, "max": 20, "step": 1, "default": 5}
preview_rows = 5
# Preview first N rows from S3 without downloading the full file
preview = head_s3(info['bucket'], "samples/clickstream_events.csv", n=preview_rows)
preview

# Compare two DataFrames (useful for before/after cleaning)
# Create a "cleaned" version by filtering out empty product_ids
import pandas as pd
clickstream_clean = clickstream[clickstream['product_id'] != ''].copy()
clickstream_clean['duration_bucket'] = pd.cut(clickstream_clean['duration_seconds'].astype(int), bins=[0, 30, 60, 120, 300], labels=['<30s', '30-60s', '1-2min', '2-5min'])

compare_df(clickstream, clickstream_clean, "original", "cleaned")

## 📊 Visualization

One-liner interactive Plotly charts. All return the figure object for further customization.

# @param {"type": "slider", "min": 3, "max": 15, "step": 1, "default": 10}
top_n_countries = 10
# Interactive bar chart
country_rev = df.groupby('shipping_country')['total'].sum().reset_index().sort_values('total', ascending=False).head(top_n_countries)
plot_bar(country_rev, x='shipping_country', y='total', title=f'Top {top_n_countries} Countries by Revenue')

# Interactive scatter plot with size and color encoding
plot_scatter(df, x='quantity', y='total', size='unit_price', color='payment_method', title='Quantity vs Total by Payment Method')

# @param {"type": "slider", "min": 5, "max": 50, "step": 5, "default": 25}
hist_bins = 25
# Interactive histogram
plot_histogram(df, 'total', bins=hist_bins, title='Order Total Distribution')

# Heatmap from a pivot (country x payment_method → revenue)
plot_heatmap(df, x='shipping_country', y='payment_method', value='total', title='Revenue: Country × Payment Method')

## 💾 Data Export

Save results back to S3 or local files.

# Save to local file (auto-detects format from extension)
to_local(summary, '/tmp/order_summary.csv')
to_local(summary, '/tmp/order_summary.parquet')
print("Saved locally ✓")

# Upload to S3
uri = to_s3_csv(summary, info['bucket'], "user-data/order_summary.csv")
print(f"Uploaded to: {uri}")

# Verify the upload
files = list_s3(info['bucket'], "user-data/")
files
